articles.expand: The core beat should support the Australian dollar and push front-end yields higher as traders trim bets on 2027 rate cuts and price in some risk of another hike. December pricing is unlikely to change much, given the weak labour market and the RBA's view that policy is already restrictive. The bigger shift is for the February meeting, which now looks more open. articles.expand: A clear beat on services inflation adds weight to December BOJ hike pricing. That should offer the yen some support and nudge short-dated JGB yields higher, especially if upcoming wage data confirms the pass-through. The yen's response may be limited while the Fed is also on a hiking path , which keeps the rate gap with the US wide and USD/JPY elevated. For equities, firmer BOJ expectations are a headwind for rate-sensitive sectors and exporters, while banks stand to benefit from higher margins. articles.title: RBA's Jacobs: five hikes have made policy clearly restrictive, but the squeeze is uneven
articles.expand: Jacobs' remarks support the market view that the RBA's tightening cycle is over, with policy now judged restrictive and housing taking the strain. That leans toward a softer Australian dollar and lower front-end yields over time. His point that a higher neutral rate may be blunting policy is a two-sided risk, though: if inflation proves sticky, it could argue against cutting as early as markets hope. Today's October CPI is the immediate test. A firm trimmed mean would strengthen the "tight on paper, less so in practice" reading and could push back pricing for 2027 cuts.
